name: Does finishing a garage interior help with home energy efficiency?

mainEntity.name: Does finishing a garage interior help with home energy efficiency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard uninsulated garages allow significant thermal transfer through shared walls and ceilings, causing adjacent living rooms or upper-floor bedrooms to stay cold in winter and hot in summer. Finishing the interior with proper insulation and sealed drywall acts as a thermal barrier, reducing your furnace and air conditioner workload. You can also seal drafts around framing plates and door openings during the drywall and trim stages. However, if your overhead garage door remains uninsulated, that single surface will still remain your largest source of ongoing heat exchange.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, insulated and drywalled garage walls create a thermal buffer that prevents drafts and reduces heating and cooling loss into adjacent rooms.
